description_full: Mesa Laboratories, Inc. develops, designs, manufactures, sells, and services life sciences tools and quality control products and services in North America, Europe, the Asia Pacific, and internationally. The Sterilization and Disinfection Control segment offers biological, chemical, and cleaning indicators, used to assess the effectiveness of sterilization, decontamination, disinfection, and cleaning processes in the pharmaceutical, medical device, and healthcare industries. This segment also provides sterility assurance testing and laboratory services to the dental and pharmaceutical industries. The Biopharmaceutical Development segment develops, manufactures, sells, and services automated systems for protein analysis (immunoassays) and peptide synthesis solutions. Its Clinical Genomics segment offers MassARRAY, a genetic analysis tool system, and related consumables, including chips, panels, and chemical reagent solutions used by clinical labs to analyze DNA samples for hereditary disease screenings, pharmacogenetics, oncology related applications, and toxicology research. The Biopharmaceutical Development segment provides automated systems, such as Gyrolab xPand and Gyrolab xPlore hardware and software, Gyrolab Bioaffy consumable microfluidic disks, Gyrolab kits and Rexxip buffers for protein analysis; and PurePep Symphony and Chorus instruments for peptide synthesis. Its Calibration Solutions segment offers quality control products to measure and calibrate critical parameters in applications, such as renal care, gas flow, environmental and process monitoring, and torque testing in pharmaceutical, laboratory, medical device, manufacturing, industrial, and environmental applications. This segment's products include continuous monitoring systems, data loggers, and torque testing systems under the DialyGuard, DryCal, DataTrace, and ViewPoint brands. Mesa Laboratories, Inc. was incorporated in 1982 and is headquartered in Lakewood, Colorado.

financial_summary: Mesa Laboratories, Inc. is a small-cap technology business with a $781M market cap on $249M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years and +11% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 1% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 61% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $40M in free cash flow — roughly 16 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 6.38× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.7× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 1.7× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.5%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 5.6% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 7% operating margin is roughly in line with the Technology median (7%).

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 69% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 4% below the high.

val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $133 (margin of safety -5%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 39%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $95.16 to $187 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Multiples send mixed signals against Technology peers: cheaper on P/FCF 19.7 vs 26.1, richer on P/E 119.8 vs 27.4 (sector median).

Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 5.1% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 2.1% (vs the 8% bar).

prof: ROIC of 1% falls short of the cost of capital of 9.4%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 80.14).
It runs a 61% gross margin and converts 16% of revenue into free cash flow, or 9% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9.
ROE of 4% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.3x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 14pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 8.2% of revenue on R&D and 7.2% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 1.7x net debt to EBITDA ($26.9M of cash against $67.5M of debt), above the 1.5x gate, and interest cover is thin at 1.7x.
Working capital ties up about 151 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
Goodwill makes up 44% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 4.4% over 3 years, 13.2% over 5 years and 11.4% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 1.0% a year of fundamental growth, too little to drive meaningful growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 2.4% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex runs only 0.6x depreciation (1.3% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 22, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 5.6%, meaningful skin in the game, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (6 sales, net $770K sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 0.5% (0.5% in dividends).
The share count has grown 1.4% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
It has paid a dividend for 22 consecutive years, raising it 2.2% a year over the last five.
people: With about 717 employees, each generates about $347K of revenue, in line with the Technology median, and revenue has grown 13.0% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $55K of free cash flow per employee.
Compensation governance scores well (3/10, lower is better).
